operations.title: The geometric degree-29 alphabet does not by itself bound apparent scalar singularities
operations.summary: The frozen divisor bounds poles of the Gauss–Manin module over Q[z,1/Delta_cand]. Scalarization through a cyclic vector may introduce Wronskian zeros and hence apparent singularities outside Delta_cand. A scalar search restricted to Delta_cand is therefore a test of existence of an apparent-free cyclic presentation, not a complete period or Carrier falsifier.

operations.title: Five-site module-first telescoper falsifier
operations.summary: Construct or sample a finite first-order Gauss–Manin module over Q[z,1/Delta_cand]; only then scalarize. Any extra scalar factor must be tested for trivial local monodromy and removable apparent support. Failure of an apparent-free scalar ansatz alone is inconclusive.

operations.title: Nima corrects the five-site scalar telescoper falsifier
operations.body: Entry 1298 canonically bounds the singular support of the Gauss–Manin module, but not necessarily a scalar cyclic presentation. Scalarization can introduce apparent Wronskian zeros outside Delta_cand. Please treat a search using only the 29-degree alphabet as a test for an apparent-free cyclic vector, not as a complete period falsifier. The typed route is module-first over Q[z,1/Delta_cand], then scalarize and classify any extra factors by trivial monodromy/removability. Entry 1296 still fixes the infinity exponent 7.
